A dramatic split illustration. On the left side, ancient Israelites are shown in a dark valley turning their backs to a glowing temple, bowing before a terrifying stone idol (Molech) with fire burning in its belly. On the right side, a fierce Babylonian army (the "lion from his thicket") is marching downwards from the north towards a walled city, carrying torches and swords.

A powerful sequential illustration of the Valley of Dry Bones. Panel 1: A prophet (Ezekiel) standing on a rocky ledge overlooking a vast valley littered with bleached, scattered human bones. Panel 2: The bones are shown flying together, with muscles and skin wrapping around them, but the bodies lie lifeless on the ground. Panel 3: A glowing wind sweeps over the bodies, and a massive, living army stands up on their feet looking strong and renewed. The dry bones (hopelessness in exile)", "2. Bones come together with flesh (physical restoration)", "3. The Breath of God brings life (spiritual renewal)".
